name: Cholamandalam Financial Holdings Ltd
title: Cholamandalam Financial Holdings Ltd - 504973 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Analyst / Investor Meet - Outcome

read.thesis: General insurance subsidiary posted Q1 FY27 combined ratio of 120.4% and PBT of Rs.116 crore; GWP grew only 6.7% with motor OD loss ratio elevated (80-86% range) and no Supreme Court motor TP provision taken.

triggers.label: Combined ratio 120.4% in Q1
triggers.quote: The combined ratio stood at 120.4%, reflecting the impact of higher motor reserve strengthening, elevated motor OD claims experience, and a large fire loss during the quarter.

triggers.label: Motor OD loss ratio not acceptable at 80-86%
triggers.quote: we are certainly not accepting the current OD loss ratio as the new normal, nor are we suggesting that a loss ratio in the range of 80% to 86% is sustainable

triggers.label: GWP growth 6.7%, GDPI 2.6%
triggers.quote: Gross written premium (GWP), on the other hand, grew by 6.7% to Rs. 2,130 crore s. While this growth was below our expectations

triggers.label: GIFT City reinsurers add soft-market capacity
triggers.quote: the emergence of GIFT City as a source of reinsurance capacity has also contributed to the current soft mar ket environment.

triggers.label: Fire industry premium down ~28%
triggers.quote: the fire line of business recorded an industry -wide decline of approximately 28% during the quarter.

summary.headline: Chola MS Q1 FY27 GWP grew 6.7% to Rs 2,130 crore, but combined ratio rose to 120.4% on motor reserving and a large fire loss.
summary.overview: Chola MS (general insurance arm) reported GDPI of Rs 1,860 crore (+2.6% YoY) and GWP of Rs 2,130 crore (+6.7%), which management said was below expectations. Claims ratio rose to 85.6% from 81.3% and combined ratio to 120.4%, driven by motor reserve strengthening, elevated motor OD claims and a large fire loss, leaving operating profit at Rs 71 crore and PBT at Rs 116 crore. Commercial lines fell 8.6% (fire down 15.5% vs industry fire decline of about 28%), and health degrew on PSU bank group platform repricing. The call was led by the new MD (in charge since June 1, 2026), who said the motor OD loss ratio of 80-86% is unacceptable and targeted a high-70s level first.

financial_highlights.value: Rs 19,000 crore / Rs 380 crore in quarter

segments.name: Motor
segments.commentary: Motor portfolio grew about 5.7%, led by commercial vehicles; mix is 48% private cars, 9.5% two-wheelers, 42.5% commercial vehicles. Motor is about 70% of the book and motor combined ratio was 128% in FY26 (123% in FY25).

segments.name: Commercial lines
segments.commentary: Portfolio declined 8.6% in Q1 on fire pricing pressure; fire decline limited to 15.5% vs industry fire decline of about 28%. Growth in marine, engineering and liability.

segments.name: Health
segments.commentary: Growth moderate; group health degrowth due to exit of gross-subsidy business and PSU bank group platform repricing and migration to retail. Network exceeds 13,000 hospitals; 99% of health claims settled within 30 days; NPS 73.

guidance_outlook: Immediate OD loss ratio target: below 80%, ideally high-70s first, then mid-70s over time; management said it would take a couple of quarters.
No provision taken in Q1 for the Supreme Court motor TP (homemaker) judgment; will await review petition outcome before deciding action.
Ind AS / IFRS implementation deferred by IRDAI one-year forbearance to April 1, 2027; no profitability impact estimate yet, expected to be shared by next quarter at the earliest.
Expects industry pricing discipline to improve in property and commercial lines after CAT losses; reinsurance market correction more likely at next renewal cycle.
Industry CAT loss estimate of Rs 3,000-4,000 crore across multiple events in Q1.
capex_capacity: Reinsurance capacity for fire and engineering secured at start of fiscal year, described as comparable to leading private players.
Motor issuance platform rolled out across bank channel; workflow enhancements under way in motor claims.
Preparing for Ind AS, Risk-Based Capital (RBC) and DPDP requirements.
demand_pricing: Industry GI growth about 8.3% in Q1 vs 8.9% last year; growth driven by motor and health, while fire saw about 28% industry decline on April renewal rate cuts.
Motor tailwinds since September 2025 supported growth; motor TP is tariff-based so premiums lag claims inflation.
Health growth moderate by design; SME and multinational single-mandate group clients targeted, retail health via bancassurance and aggregators.
Inward reinsurance growth tied to commercial line pitches and group health; management did not quantify its share.
Reinsurance soft market attributed partly to GIFT City capacity; management expects correction at next renewal.

qa_highlights.question: Has the company provided additionally for motor TP given the Supreme Court housewife judgment, and what is the path for motor OD loss ratio?
qa_highlights.answer: No provision taken in Q1 for the Supreme Court judgment; review petition pending. OD loss ratio is not accepted as the new normal; immediate target is high-70s, then mid-70s over time, with improvement expected over a couple of quarters.

qa_highlights.question: Why is retail health declining while the industry grows robustly?
qa_highlights.answer: Group health decline reflects exit of gross-subsidy business and repricing of PSU bank group platform pockets with claims leakage; some migration to retail platform. Retail health needs capability building and patience.

qa_highlights.question: Is the motor loss ratio increase driven by new book or reserve under-provisioning?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is not purely reserve strengthening; increase reflects claims inflation assumptions in reserving, and TP premiums are tariff-based so do not keep pace.

qa_highlights.question: What is the financial impact of an adverse Supreme Court outcome on solvency?
qa_highlights.answer: Reserves said to be prudent with margin for adverse deviation; impact would be considered within that framework if required. Scenarios such as prospective-only application remain open; no quantification given.

qa_highlights.question: Will IFRS/Ind AS change profitability and ROE?
qa_highlights.answer: Forbearance granted; implementation from April 1, 2027. Special-purpose financial statements not yet submitted; no reliable estimate of impact, to be shared possibly next quarter.

qa_highlights.question: What is the source of inward reinsurance growth and is it sustainable?
qa_highlights.answer: Two parts: commercial lines pitches where the company takes reinsurance share, and selective group health participation. Sustainability not quantified.

qa_highlights.question: Will CAT-driven pricing discipline help the current year and how much did GIFT City affect soft reinsurance market?
qa_highlights.answer: Pricing discipline more likely in next year as reinsurance renewal, not current year; GIFT City capacity has contributed to softness and sustainability depends on reinsurer returns.

risks_watch: Motor OD loss ratio elevated (80-86% range); corrective measures expected to take a couple of quarters.
Supreme Court motor TP judgment and review petition outcome; potential retrospective provisioning and solvency impact (currently 1.93x).
Health portfolio profitability and group health degrowth; retail health capability build-out.
Reinsurance renewal terms, capacity and retention after current treaties; soft market from GIFT City capacity.
Ind AS transition from April 1, 2027 and RBC framework readiness; profitability impact undisclosed.
Management said a Rs 12.4 crore net fire loss was one-off in the quarter, but CAT losses could raise deductibles across events.
summary.management_tone: Candid and cautious: management openly called the motor OD loss ratio unacceptable and conceded health and commercial lines are under pressure. Forward-looking statements on recovery are hedged with timelines of a couple of quarters, and management declined to quantify Supreme Court, IFRS and reinsurance impacts.
key_quotes: we are certainly not accepting the current OD loss ratio as the new normal, nor are we suggesting that a loss ratio in the range of 80% to 86% is sustainable
We have not taken any provision during the quarter in relation to the Supreme Court judgment.
our immediate objective is to bring the OD loss ratio down to a level that begins with a "7", ideally in the high-70s to start with.
Consequently, if an insurer has a catastrophe deductible of, say, Rs.20 crore or Rs.25 crore, that deductible may need to be absorbed separately for each incident

growth.why: Management gave no revenue growth guidance; GWP grew 6.7% YoY and was below expectations, with the immediate focus on margin repair (OD loss ratio to high-70s) rather than growth, and no capacity additions or order-book backing were described.

mgmt.note: New MD in charge since June 1, 2026 called the motor OD loss ratio unacceptable and targeted a high-70s level first; no specific growth plan given.
